messages:
maria: Heads up — p95 spiked on /generate (standard tier) after yesterday's kernel selection tweak. Quick profile shows larger microbatches with high KV hit ratios causing head-of-line blocking.

ajay: Seen it, curious if it's the kernel change or the queue policy interacting with token budgets. Got the flamegraph?

maria: Pasted flame sample + tail logs below. Most time is in merge_pending_batches and serialize_kv_cache. Notably, requests that hit the cache still occupy batch slots for full token budgets.

kevin: Can you drop the hot snippet?

maria: ```
# flame sample (condensed)
merge_pending_batches 40%
serialize_kv_cache 22%
kernel_dispatch 18%
other 20%
```

elaine: Nice find. If KV hits short-circuit generation, we should reduce token_budget for cached routes so they don't hog the batch. Suggest dynamic budgeter by route + tier.

sam: Agreed. Also the queue policy currently prioritizes size over age; large cached requests wait to fill token budget leading to p95 tail. Maybe switch to age-first for 'standard' routes.

ajay: Proposed simple change: when kv_hit_ratio > 0.6, set effective_token_budget = max(64, configured_budget * 0.3). Also, for standard tier, queue_policy: age_then_size with max_wait_ms=25.

kevin: I prototyped that locally. Microbench with synthetic KV-hit trace: p95 improved from 210ms -> 140ms, throughput ~-2%.

maria: Can you post the exact config snippet you used?

kevin: ```yaml
batching: 
  queue_policy: age_then_size
  max_wait_ms: 25
token_budget_policy:
  dynamic_by_route_tier: true
  overrides:
    routes:
      "/generate":
        standard: 512
        premium: 1024
    kv_hit_multiplier: 0.3
    min_budget: 64
```

elaine: Looks reasonable. Two concerns: (1) rollout safety — need canary on a small % of standard traffic, (2) kernel fallback if budget too small for certain models (avoid under-provisioning).

maria: Plan: roll canary at 2% on standard for 30m with tracing on microbatch sizes and token budgets. If p95 improves and throughput drop <5% -> 10% -> full. Canary config and monitors in the dashboard.

runtime-bot: deploy:canary started by maria — 2% on standard routes. Link: https://internal.redwood/dev/deploys/1825678901

ajay: I'll add a regression alert for kernel_dispatch latency >= +15% and a p95 guard for user-facing latency.

sam: Also add perf counters for kv_hold_duration (how long a request holds batch slot while waiting) — should go to ops.

kevin: One extra note: some request patterns with long contexts still benefit from larger budgets. We should make the dynamic multiplier sensitive to seq_len distribution (e.g., multiplier = 0.3 for short <256, 0.6 for 256-1024).

maria: Good call. Update to the policy: multiplier_by_len. I'll draft PR with canary flags + dashboard links.

elaine: Thanks — quick triage. If canary looks good, schedule follow-up to bake kernel fallbacks into the allocator (auto-increase budget when kernel signals low throughput).

maria: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infr/proposals/1234 — includes telemetry, config, and rollout steps. Will ping after initial canary metrics. :thumbsup:

sam: Nice work team.
